incidents.victim: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor with admin access created a public GitHub repo named 'Private-CISA' and disabled GitHub's built-in secret-scanning protections before publishing plaintext credentials, AWS GovCloud admin keys, an RSA private key for a CISA-IT GitHub App, and internal system logs.
incidents.impact: Exposed administrative credentials to three AWS GovCloud accounts and dozens of internal CISA systems including the agency's 'Landing Zone DevSecOps' environment, giving any opportunistic attacker a roadmap to federal networks; more than a week after notification CISA was still working to invalidate keys, and lawmakers including Sen. Hassan and Rep. Thompson have demanded answers.

incidents.vector: Attacker compromised an end-of-life Azure-hosted F5 BIG-IP load balancer, pivoted via SSH to an internal Linux host, then exploited an unpatched Atlassian Confluence server to obtain credentials and launched Kerberos relay attacks (CVE-2025-33073) against Active Directory.
incidents.impact: Multi-stage Linux intrusion cascaded from a perimeter appliance to credential theft and lateral movement against domain infrastructure; Microsoft published the case to warn that EOL edge appliances and unpatched internal Confluence servers are now common ingress for identity-centric, multi-domain attack chains.

incidents.victim: Technology sector workers in U.S., Israel, UAE and two other Middle Eastern entities
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing recruitment lures impersonating an airline and a video conferencing platform delivered DLL-sideloaded payloads; new MiniUpdate and MiniJunk V2 RAT variants used AppDomainManager hijacking to disable .NET security mechanisms and route C2 through 3-5 rotating Azure-hosted domains per target.
incidents.impact: Six new RAT variants deployed against high-value tech professionals between mid-February and April, coinciding with the regional conflict that began Feb 28, 2026; Unit 42 assesses moderate-high confidence the campaign supports Iranian intelligence collection on aerospace, defense and telecom targets.

incidents.victim: Government organizations in Belgium, Italy, Serbia, Spain, Poland and South Africa
incidents.vector: Initial access via vulnerability scanning of internet-facing assets followed by deployment of two new custom backdoors — EchoCreep (uses Discord servers for C2) and GraphWorm (uses Microsoft Graph/OneDrive for C2) — plus SoftEther VPN and custom SOCKS proxies to tunnel traffic and evade detection.
incidents.impact: ESET research details a China-aligned APT pivoting from Asian to European government targets, abusing trusted SaaS endpoints (Discord, Microsoft Graph, Amazon S3) for command-and-control to blend with legitimate traffic; analysts say the actor is searching for pivot points to burrow deeper for espionage.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Defense and other DDoS victims
incidents.vector: Operator built and ran the Kimwolf IoT botnet, enslaving millions of devices traditionally firewalled from the internet (digital photo frames, web cameras) and renting them out for record-setting DDoS attacks issued via over 25,000 attack commands.
incidents.impact: Canadian police arrested 23-year-old Jacob Butler ('Dort') in Ottawa on a U.S. extradition warrant; Kimwolf was tied to attacks measured at nearly 30 Tbps — a record DDoS volume — that affected DoD IP ranges and caused some victims more than $1M in losses. Earlier infrastructure seizures in March took down Kimwolf alongside botnets Aisuru, JackSkid and Mossad.

incidents.vector: Kali365 phishing-as-a-service platform (sold on Telegram for $250/month to $2,000/year) uses AI-generated lures impersonating Adobe, DocuSign and SharePoint to trick victims into completing Microsoft's legitimate OAuth device-code login flow, granting attacker-controlled apps persistent access without intercepting credentials or MFA codes.
incidents.impact: FBI public service announcement Thursday warned of hundreds of Kali365-enabled attacks since April; captured OAuth access and refresh tokens give immediate, MFA-bypassing access to Outlook, Teams and OneDrive and have been reused by other criminals for mailbox theft, BEC, lateral phishing and post-compromise extortion.

incidents.victim: German university hospitals (Cologne, Freiburg, Heidelberg, Tübingen, Ulm, Mannheim) via billing provider Unimed
incidents.vector: Unknown hackers breached Unimed, a third-party that handles billing for privately insured and self-paying patients at numerous German hospitals; the attackers exfiltrated patient billing and demographic data without touching hospital clinical infrastructure.
incidents.impact: University Hospital Cologne reported ~30,000 affected (with health-related details exposed in 840+ cases and bank/payment data in five), Freiburg ~54,000 (900 with diagnosis/treatment information), Heidelberg ~11,000 (2,700 with billing data), Ulm ~1,600; hospitals halted data transfers, filed criminal complaints and are weighing legal action against Unimed.

incidents.victim: Telecommunications providers and ISPs in Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, the Middle East and disputed Donbas region
incidents.vector: Multiple Chinese threat clusters deployed 'Showboat' (a.k.a. 'kworker'), a previously undetected Linux post-exploitation framework with LAN-scanning capabilities to reach internal devices isolated from the public internet; one operator paired it with the JFMBackdoor Windows implant.
incidents.impact: Black Lotus Labs and PwC found Showboat has enabled years of stealthy espionage against small-market telcos in Central Asia and beyond, with zero VirusTotal detections at the time of discovery; analysts say its presence usually signals a much deeper compromise of the surrounding network.

incidents.vector: A GitHub employee installed the malicious Nx Console VS Code extension — itself compromised in the May 11 TanStack supply-chain attack — which executed an attacker payload that exfiltrated internal repository contents.
incidents.impact: More than 3,800 of GitHub's internal code repositories were stolen and listed for sale on a hacking forum; GitHub is rotating critical secret tokens to prevent follow-on access. The same TanStack-derived compromise was named as the source of an intrusion at Grafana days earlier.

incidents.vector: Compromise traced to the same TanStack npm/Nx Console supply-chain incident that hit GitHub, in which a malicious VS Code extension was used as initial access.
incidents.impact: Grafana publicly named the TanStack incident as the source of its breach; full scope of accessed data has not been disclosed but the company is responding alongside other affected dependents of the wave.

incidents.vector: Specific intrusion method not disclosed; the ShinyHunters extortion group listed the company on its dark web leak site.
incidents.impact: 7-Eleven disclosed an April data breach to Maine's Attorney General after ShinyHunters posted the company on its leak site; details on the scope of stolen customer data remain limited.

incidents.victim: Government of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack against government email infrastructure; officials have not yet specified whether the incident involved ransomware.
incidents.impact: Disrupted email servers across the CNMI government and is expected to slow administrative operations for the U.S. Pacific territory.

incidents.vector: Account takeovers of legitimate BlueSky users — exact compromise vector not disclosed — followed by posting of attacker-controlled content from trusted handles.
incidents.impact: Hijacked accounts were used to push pro-Kremlin and anti-Ukraine propaganda from a known Russian disinformation outfit; BlueSky has been suspending compromised accounts pending owner recovery.

incidents.victim: Pierre & Vacances, Belambra, Gîtes de France
incidents.vector: Specific intrusion vector unspecified; an actor calling themselves 'ChimeraZ' claimed all three breaches and posted the stolen data for sale.
incidents.impact: Customer data from three major French holiday-booking sites is now circulating in cybercrime markets, exposing affected travelers to fraud and phishing follow-on.

incidents.vector: Exploit against the Verus-Ethereum bridge protocol; technical root cause not yet publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole approximately $11.58 million in crypto assets from the bridge, adding to a long string of DeFi bridge exploits.

incidents.victim: RXNT (and U.S. Congress members served by its e-prescription service)
incidents.vector: RXNT — which handles drug prescriptions including for members of the U.S. Congress — was breached in March 2026 by unidentified attackers who exfiltrated patient data.
incidents.impact: Patient data including for U.S. lawmakers was stolen; RXNT notified authorities on the final day allowed under U.S. health privacy laws, raising questions about the company's disclosure practices.

incidents.victim: TanStack, OpenSearch, UiPath, Mistral AI and 165+ other npm/PyPI projects (520M cumulative weekly downloads in scope)
incidents.vector: First documented Shai-Hulud wave needing no stolen credential: attackers chained a GitHub Actions 'Pwn Request' (pull_request_target with checkout of fork merge ref) with cache poisoning of a 1.1GB pnpm store and OIDC token extraction from runner /proc/<pid>/mem to publish 84 malicious packages with valid SLSA Build Level 3 provenance.
incidents.impact: Within hours, 373 malicious versions across 169 npm packages plus PyPI packages were published — including the official OpenSearch JavaScript client, 57 UiPath automation packages and Mistral AI's TypeScript client — propagating credential theft and CI/CD pipeline backdoors across the ecosystem; the worm's source code was publicly released May 12, already spawning copycat activity.
